pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Darkening of the urine to a port-wine hue upon UV/light exposure (due to porphobilinogen auto-oxidation into porphobilin), triggered by fasting and sulfonamide administration. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: AIP is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by a deficiency of porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD) in the heme biosynthesis pathway. When the liver requires upregulated heme synthesis—precipitated here by severe caloric restriction and CYP-inducing medications (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole)—the rate-limiting enzyme ALAS1 ramps up production. The metabolic roadblock at PBGD causes a massive, toxic accumulation of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). ALA is directly neurotoxic, inducing autonomic hyperreactivity (tachycardia, malignant hypertension, visceral abdominal spasm without peritoneal inflammation), hypothalamic SIADH (severe hyponatremia), central neuropsychiatric collapse (hallucinations, seizures), and peripheral motor axonal neuropathy (ascending paralysis mimicking Guillain-Barré syndrome).
